sections.h2: Anne Arundel County at a glance
sections.html: Anne Arundel County sits south of Baltimore on the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay, with Annapolis as both county seat and state capital. The 2020 census counted 588,261 residents. Of the county's 588 square miles, 173 (29 percent) are water, so creeks, rivers and shoreline shape much of the housing. Fort Meade, the airport at BWI, and state government keep demand for homes steady, and commuters can reach Baltimore and Washington by road, light rail or MARC.

Maryland's Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) reassessed the county for January 1, 2026. The figures show how much value moved across three years.

Measure (Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2026)Anne Arundel County
Combined full cash value$46.52 billion to $53.53 billion (up 15.1%)
Residential value$31.23 billion to $36.24 billion (up 16.0%)
Commercial value$15.28 billion to $17.29 billion (up 13.1%)
Residential properties that rose in value98.98%

An increase phases in evenly over three years, and a decrease takes full effect in the 2026 tax year. You can appeal within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. The appeal goes first to SDAT, then to the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then to the Maryland Tax Court. The homestead credit limits yearly growth in the taxable assessment of a principal residence, with a state cap of 10 percent and lower limits in some local governments.

Bills are mailed in July to the address on file with SDAT. Tax is due without interest as of July 1, and the payment deadline is September 30. Owners of a principal residence can split the bill into two installments, due September 30 and December 31.

For fiscal year 2027, July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, the county adds a 0.87 percent service charge to the balance of the second installment. State law allows up to 1.65 percent, so the county sits below the ceiling. Pay the whole bill by September 30 and you skip the charge.

  • State rate: $0.112 per $100 of taxable assessment.
  • City of Annapolis rate: $0.738 per $100, for addresses inside the city.
  • Escrowed owners who want to pay annually should tell their lender by May 1.
  • Homestead credit applications are due December 31 and take effect from July 1 of the following year.

Call the Real Property Tax Division for the county rate that applies to your address before you estimate a bill.

The Real Property Tax Division, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, answers billing questions. It is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at (410) 222-1736 or realproperty@aacounty.org. SDAT handles values and ownership records.

  • Finance Department customer service: (410) 222-1144.
  • Land Records, for deeds and liens: (410) 222-1425.
  • SDAT, for ownership and mailing address changes: (410) 974-5709.
  • Cashier's offices, including Glen Burnie: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. After hours, sealed check payments can go in the yellow drop-off box and are processed the next business day.

If you paid a bill on a property you no longer own, contact the office about a possible refund. Credit balances from adjusted bills are refunded as soon as possible.

A deed carries a county recordation tax of $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500. The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. The Recordation and Transfer Tax Division collects both, and every instrument that might be subject to them must be endorsed by that office before it is recorded.

Checks are payable to Anne Arundel County. State transfer tax and recording fees go through the Land Records Office at (410) 222-1425, and e-recording is available. The county posts claim-for-refund forms for both taxes and an affidavit form for certain transactions. Which side pays each tax is set in the sales contract, so ask your title company to itemize it before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Waterfront sellers and the Critical Area
sections.html:
The Critical Area is the land and water within 1,000 feet of tidal waters, and in this county it can change what a buyer may do with a lot.

  • The Buffer extends 100 feet landward from tidal waters, tributary stream banks and tidal wetland boundaries. Disturbing it generally takes an approved variance.
  • Removing any tree or vegetation, even a dead tree, requires an approved Vegetation Management Plan.
  • Grading disturbances over 5,000 square feet need a grading permit.
  • In limited development and resource conservation areas, impervious surface is capped at 15 to 31 percent of the site.

The county's Critical Area Planner of the Day is at the Heritage Complex, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, (410) 222-7960. If you have a pier, deck or bulkhead near the water, collect the permits on file before listing, and ask your title company whether any disclosure applies.

Unpaid Maryland property tax becomes a lien the county can sell at a tax sale, held in June on a date the Controller sets. The owner keeps the property after the sale, but the buyer receives a tax lien certificate and the right to foreclose if the debt stays unpaid.

Before a sale, the collector must mail notice at least 30 days before the property is first advertised, and the advertisement runs weekly for four weeks. A buyer may file a foreclosure complaint six months after the sale, or nine months for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate is void if no foreclosure action follows within two years. Redemption interest runs 1.5 percent per month, so waiting raises the payoff.

Limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners may qualify for help through the state's Homeowner Protection Program. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman meets by appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore.

A balance does not prevent a sale, but it must be handled at or before closing. Call the Real Property Tax Division for the amount, and act before the June tax sale if you are behind. The title company can pay the county from your proceeds.

  1. Ask the division for a payoff figure for every open bill.
  2. Collect permits for any waterfront structures and any Critical Area approvals.
  3. Ask the title company to itemize the recordation and transfer taxes.
  4. Close, and let the title company send the county its payment from the proceeds.

We buy houses as is, so you do not have to clear violations or repair a bulkhead first. Call or text with the address and we will tell you what we can offer.

faqs.q: When are Anne Arundel County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due without interest as of July 1 and must be paid by September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and the balance by December 31.

faqs.q: What is the semiannual service charge in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2027 the county adds 0.87 percent to the balance of the second installment. Paying the full amount by September 30 avoids it.

faqs.q: How do I appeal an Anne Arundel County assessment?
faqs.a: File with SDAT within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. If you disagree with the result, the next steps are the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and then the Maryland Tax Court.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. The recordation tax is $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500.

faqs.q: Does the Critical Area affect selling a house near the water?
faqs.a: It can. Land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters is in the Critical Area, which carries a 100 foot buffer, vegetation plan rules and grading permit thresholds a buyer may need to understand.
